about.text: Mursik is a traditional fermented milk variant of the Kalenjin people of Kenya. It can be made from cow or goat milk and is fermented in a specially made calabash gourd locally known as a sotet. The gourd is lined with soot from specific trees, such as the African senna, which add flavor to the fermented milk. It is normally consumed with ugali or on its own and is served at room temperature or chilled.

how.text: Lactic acid bacteria and yeasts sour the milk in a gourd lined with charcoal dust. The charcoal absorbs the 'cowy' flavours of fresh milk, adds its own smoky taste and turns the milk the bluish-grey colour that Kalenjin farmers prize.
